images.caption: View of the Cable Depot, built in 1882-83 as part of the General Post Office submarine cable depot. It contains/contained four circular 11m-diameter cast-iron tanks on 92cm-thick concrete foundations where submarine telegraph cables were stored under water. It is now used as a car parts store. These sheds represented a missing link in the Thames Path which made a diversion inland to get round them (mended in 2018). Photographed in 2006 from the disused ferry jetty alongside.
images.alt: View of the Cable Depot, built in 1882-83 as part of the General Post Office submarine cable depot. It contains/contained four circular 11m-diameter cast-iron tanks on 92cm-thick concrete foundations where submarine telegraph cables were stored under water. It is now used as a car parts store. images.filename: Steps over the flood barrier near Woolwich - geograph.org.uk - 1454749.jpg
images.caption: Steps over the flood barrier near Woolwich Downstream of the Thames barrier a continuous flood defence level has to be maintained along each side of the river to protect low-lying properties; in some places that means having an artificial barrier across the Thames Path.  Here, the flood defence level is represented by a brick wall and the path crosses it by means of this 'designer' set of steps and by a zig-zag cycle ramp [link].
